question: A 40-year-old woman with cervical cancer has a tumour that is 5 cm in its greatest dimension, with biopsy-confirmed right parametrial invasion but no extension to the pelvic side wall. Pelvic MRI confirms no involvement of the lower one-third of the vagina. CT chest/abdomen is clear. According to the FIGO 2018 staging system, what is her stage?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. FIGO 2018 Stage IIB = parametrial invasion without extension to the pelvic side wall. Size is not the defining criterion once parametrial spread is present.
Incorrect. Stage IIIB requires extension to the pelvic side wall or hydronephrosis/non-functioning kidney — neither is present here.
Incorrect. Stage IIA2 means upper two-thirds vaginal involvement with tumour >4 cm but no parametrial spread. This patient has parametrial invasion, which moves her to Stage II-B or beyond.
Incorrect. Stage IVA indicates invasion of the bladder or rectal mucosa. There is no mucosal invasion in this scenario.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review FIGO 2018 cervical staging: Stage IIB is defined by parametrial invasion that has not yet reached the pelvic side wall.
Well done. Parametrial invasion (without pelvic wall extension) = FIGO 2018 Stage IIB.
